speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension; can you tell me if you have noticed any vomiting, particularly if it is forceful or projectile?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Has the vomiting ever been green or yellowish, and has he passed any stool at all recently? Also, when you gently press on his abdomen, does he retract the skin or does it remain firm and tense?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Palpation; REQUEST TEST: Blood_Gas_Analysis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Abdominal_Palpation: Abdomen is soft but distended, with crying intensifying on palpation especially in the left lower quadrant; Blood_Gas_Analysis: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text:
Did you notice if he is passing gas, and does the skin over the distended area look shiny or stretched? Also, has he had any episodes of passing stool that was very foul-smelling or contained mucus?

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound; REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray (if not already reviewed in detail). Has the baby passed any stool at all, or is his bowel movement completely absent?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Hypertrophic Pyloric Stenosis
